claim: A positive response to a tap test or temporary drainage can enrich the probability of postoperative response, but the test protocols, assessment timing, and response thresholds are heterogeneous; a negative result does not safely exclude shunt responsiveness.
contradicting_reviews: FT-011 and FT-029 describe inconsistent performance across individual modalities/series.
independence_concern: European/Dutch/Japanese drainage cohorts recur across several reviews; apparent replication is partly non-independent.
certainty: LOW to MODERATE for sensitivity; LOW/VERY LOW for specificity depending on test and synthesis
can_rule_in: PARTIAL — a clearly positive, objectively measured response may support selection when concordant with clinical/imaging evidence.
can_rule_out: NO — negative TT should not be a stand-alone exclusion criterion.
changes_surgical_decision: Supports multidisciplinary selection and may change confidence, not automatically determine surgery.
counseling_implication: Explain that the test is probabilistic and protocol-dependent; nonresponse does not prove absence of potential benefit.
research_need: Prospective all-comers cohorts, prespecified multidomain MCID/reliable-change criteria, and surgery irrespective of index-test result to reduce partial verification bias.

domain: Lumbar infusion / resistance to CSF outflow
claim: Higher Rout is associated with greater odds of shunt response in some syntheses, but cutoffs and operating characteristics vary and negative predictive value is insufficient for exclusion.
contradicting_reviews: FT-011 reports no consistently superior invasive or non-invasive technique; several primary studies in FT-044 found limited incremental value.
independence_concern: Dutch and European multicentre cohorts are repeatedly reused; threshold analyses within FT-044 overlap heavily.
can_rule_in: PARTIAL — an abnormal Rout may strengthen the case in a compatible phenotype.
can_rule_out: NO — normal/low Rout cannot reliably rule out response.
changes_surgical_decision: May refine probability when local expertise exists; should not be an isolated gatekeeper.
counseling_implication: Discuss invasive burden and the possibility of response despite a negative/low-threshold result.
research_need: Uniform infusion methods, externally validated thresholds, independent cohorts, and models combining Rout with clinical, imaging, and drainage-response data.

domain: Extended lumbar drainage and intracranial pressure monitoring
claim: ELD and selected ICP-monitoring metrics showed comparatively strong diagnostic signals in some reviews, but estimates arise from small, selected cohorts with verification and spectrum-bias concerns.
contradicting_reviews: FT-011 found insufficient evidence to establish one optimal predictive technique.
independence_concern: Several reviews share historical specialized-center cohorts; exact independence is not fully verified.
can_rule_in: PARTIAL — a positive ELD/ICPM result may materially increase confidence.
can_rule_out: NO — evidence is insufficient to use a negative result as a universal contraindication.
changes_surgical_decision: Consider mainly in diagnostically uncertain patients at experienced centers, balancing invasiveness and complication risk.
counseling_implication: Clarify that higher apparent accuracy may partly reflect patient selection and reference-standard verification.
research_need: Prospective head-to-head comparisons with standardized reference outcomes, complete shunt verification, harms reporting, and decision-curve analysis.

claim: No single imaging marker consistently and strongly discriminates responders. Callosal angle and periventricular white-matter changes reached statistical significance in one meta-analysis but with weak diagnostic effect; DESH and other markers were inconsistent.
contradicting_reviews: FT-028 reported weak statistical discrimination for callosal angle/PVWM; FT-029 found no repeatedly consistent imaging parameter.
independence_concern: The same imaging cohorts and publications appear in multiple reviews; independence is limited.
can_rule_in: NO — imaging alone is insufficient to rule in clinically meaningful benefit.
can_rule_out: NO — absence of DESH, narrow callosal angle, or other single sign should not automatically exclude surgery.
changes_surgical_decision: Use imaging to support diagnosis, exclude alternatives, and contribute to a multimodal probability estimate rather than as a solitary selection rule.
counseling_implication: Counsel that characteristic imaging increases diagnostic plausibility but does not guarantee postoperative improvement.
research_need: Standardized acquisition/measurement, blinded thresholds, domain-specific outcomes, external validation, and incremental value beyond clinical/drainage tests.

domain: Biomarkers, Alzheimer pathology, and complex iNPH
claim: CSF/venous biomarkers and Alzheimer-related pathology may be associated with postoperative outcome, especially cognition, but no biomarker has shown sufficiently robust sensitivity and specificity for stand-alone selection and no formal treatment-effect modification was established.
contradicting_reviews: FT-030 and FT-039 emphasize inconsistent or insufficient evidence for many biomarkers.
independence_concern: Substantial overlap among biopsy/CSF biomarker cohorts is probable; exact cohort linkage remains incompletely verified.
can_rule_in: NO — biomarker positivity cannot by itself identify certain beneficiaries.
can_rule_out: NO — comorbidity or Alzheimer-associated biomarkers should not be interpreted as proof of no shunt benefit.
changes_surgical_decision: Primarily modifies counseling, expected domain profile, and uncertainty rather than creating an absolute surgical contraindication.
counseling_implication: Explain that gait or urinary benefit may still occur even when cognitive recovery is limited by comorbidity.
research_need: Prospective multimodal biomarker cohorts, standardized pathology definitions, domain-specific MCIDs, and formal treatment-by-marker interaction using an appropriate non-shunted comparator where ethically feasible.

claim: Complex iNPH may have lower or more uncertain global response than pure iNPH, but available comparative evidence is imprecise and does not demonstrate absence of benefit; associations are prognostic, not causal treatment-effect modifiers.
contradicting_reviews: FT-003 found several complex-versus-pure comparisons non-significant under prespecified models.
independence_concern: Phenotype definitions and cohorts overlap; adjustment for confounding is inconsistent.
can_rule_in: NO — no single comorbidity or symptom pattern reliably rules in benefit.
can_rule_out: NO — diabetes, neurodegenerative overlap, atypical manifestations, or incomplete triad should not automatically rule out shunting.
changes_surgical_decision: Changes the expected magnitude/domain of response and the consent discussion more than the binary decision alone.
counseling_implication: Set domain-specific expectations and distinguish potentially reversible iNPH symptoms from comorbidity-related limitations.
research_need: Harmonized phenotype criteria, multivariable prognostic models, external validation, and reporting of absolute domain-specific benefit and harms.

claim: Gait is the most consistently responsive domain, but instruments, task conditions, timing, and thresholds vary substantially; statistical change or group mean improvement is not equivalent to an individual MCID.
contradicting_reviews: FT-020/FT-056 show methodological heterogeneity that limits direct comparison.
independence_concern: Primary gait cohorts recur across measurement reviews; many studies are cross-sectional or small.
certainty: MODERATE for postoperative gait improvement; LOW for any specific predictive cutoff
can_rule_in: PARTIAL — reproducible objective gait improvement after drainage can support selection.
can_rule_out: NO — absence of change on one gait metric or at one time point does not conclusively exclude later or domain-specific benefit.
changes_surgical_decision: Use a prespecified battery and repeated measurement rather than subjective gait impression alone.
counseling_implication: Explain learning effects, day-to-day variability, and delayed improvement; interpret change against validated/reliable thresholds when available.
research_need: Consensus core outcome set, iNPH-specific MCIDs/reliable-change indices, wearable validation, and standardized post-drainage timing.

claim: Cognitive and neuropsychiatric improvement occurs in a subset, but reported instruments and definitions are heterogeneous and often based on statistical or author-defined change rather than validated individual clinical importance.
contradicting_reviews: FT-002/FT-041 report variable or domain-dependent cognitive effects; atypical/neuropsychiatric evidence is sparse.
independence_concern: Repeated small neuropsychological cohorts and overlapping instruments may inflate apparent breadth.
can_rule_in: NO — baseline cognitive profile alone does not reliably identify certain responders.
can_rule_out: NO — severe or atypical cognitive/neuropsychiatric features require differential diagnosis but are not an evidence-based absolute exclusion in these reviews.
changes_surgical_decision: Use domain-specific testing and avoid defining success solely by MMSE or group-level mean change.
counseling_implication: Counsel that gait may improve more reliably than cognition and that comorbid neurodegeneration may limit cognitive recovery.
research_need: Prospective cognitive core battery, reliable-change/MCID criteria, assessor blinding, and longer follow-up with competing neurodegenerative diagnoses characterized.

domain: Function, quality of life, and patient/caregiver perception
claim: Functional independence and quality of life can improve after shunting, but patient-reported and caregiver-reported outcomes are underused and definitions are inconsistent.
contradicting_reviews: No included review provides a uniformly validated patient-centered response definition across cohorts.
independence_concern: Outcome cohorts overlap with general shunt-outcome literature; reporting is selective.
changes_surgical_decision: Add patient goals, caregiver observations, functional independence, and quality of life to the response framework rather than relying only on clinician-rated triad scores.
counseling_implication: Frame benefit around activities meaningful to the patient and acknowledge that domain improvements may diverge.
research_need: Validated iNPH patient-reported outcome measures, goal-attainment endpoints, caregiver instruments, and prespecified MCIDs.

domain: Sustained benefit, complications, reoperation, and net benefit
claim: Early response does not guarantee sustained benefit, and complication/reoperation rates materially affect net clinical benefit; reviews use heterogeneous follow-up and older versus contemporary surgical cohorts. Baseline functional severity is also associated with long-term survival among shunted patients.
contradicting_reviews: FT-053 reports high historical complication/reoperation ranges, whereas more contemporary series/reviews generally report better outcomes; direct comparability is limited.
independence_concern: Historical cohorts recur across reviews and surgical technology/selection evolved over time.
certainty: LOW to MODERATE for the existence of benefit/harms; LOW for individualized long-term prediction
changes_surgical_decision: The decision should integrate expected domain-specific benefit, durability, frailty/comorbidity, valve strategy, and the risk of revision/complication.
counseling_implication: Provide separate estimates for early response, sustained response, complications, and reoperation; avoid presenting response probability without harms.
research_need: Contemporary prospective registries with standardized long-term outcomes, competing-risk analysis, valve/shunt details, and individualized net-benefit prediction.

claim: Worse baseline gait, continence, and mRS are associated with shorter survival after shunting, but this does not establish that earlier surgery causally improves survival.
contradicting_reviews: None directly; only two primary studies informed severity-stratified survival
independence_concern: Two Swedish cohorts may overlap; IPD were reconstructed from published Kaplan–Meier curves.
changes_surgical_decision: Supports counseling and urgency assessment, not a binary selection threshold.
counseling_implication: Discuss long-term prognosis separately from expected symptomatic response and operative benefit.
research_need: Prospective all-comers cohorts comparing early versus delayed surgery with causal methods and patient-centered outcomes.
